scene.picture: Pixel-art particle simulation on a near-black blue-tinted ground. Title "NUCLEAR FISSION" in a white bitmap font over one big glowing green nucleus (a cluster of small green balls with a soft dark-green halo), label U-235 under it, a tiny white neutron streaks in from the left. The nucleus splits into a pink (BA) and a blue (KR) nucleus that fly apart, firing 2-3 neutron dots. The view pulls back to a regular lattice of small green nuclei (each a 3-tone pixel ball, highlight top-left). A caption panel at the top and a counter panel under it (dark navy fill, 1 art-pixel green-tinted border, small corner ticks) show GENERATION n and a big splits count that doubles every half second (8, 64, 1,024, 131,072, then scientific notation 4.4x10^12 ... 6.0x10^23). Each split spawns pink and blue fragments; the lattice fills with fragment dots, a ring of orange-rimmed reacting nuclei spreads outward, and finally a dark-red then orange pixel fireball grows out of the middle.
